title: The Educated Barbarian: Meditations analysis (part. 8)
summary: Part 8 of NH's Meditations reading, centred on change. He covers time as a river returning to its source, good always outlasting evil, imagining your own failure, questioning rather than accepting truths, not fearing the date of death, being an unbreakable promontory, reframing misfortune as victory, and taking the short (hard, straight) way.
claims: Things that change can move from evil to good, so evil in anything changing can only last a moment
Time is a river carrying us toward death; stepping out of it would mean leaving society and losing the ability to be good, since goodness is help given to others
Like water returning to its source, the river keeps going after your death; everything in it, past and future, is connected
Good keeps renewing itself in every new person, so evil can never fully suppress it; good is like a fire that reignites from an ember
Imagining yourself going astray, as you would rehearse death, prepares you to resist failure and to handle it if it comes
Humans are born to question truths; an accepted but unquestioned truth is not understood and is worthless, and rejecting a truth at least teaches you something
Fussing over dying a day sooner is cowardice; do not obsess over when death comes, and do not waste the days you could spend living
Be unbreakable like a promontory against waves: not avoiding or whining about trouble, but inviting it
Trouble comes to everyone; your ability to destroy it when it hits makes you strong, and each round makes you stronger
Taking pride that others would not have endured what you did is slightly impure but natural; the goal is to be a survivor
Reframe misfortune: celebrate conquering the incident instead of mourning it, and over time your mind learns to enjoy challenges
The short way is the straight path, which is often the hard way (10 meters of poison ivy beats a mile of flat ground); take it without dodging
